packs.name: Romantasy
packs.hint: A love story and a fantasy plot that carry each other, with guides, character templates and worldbuilding.

notes.title: The promises of romantasy
notes.body:
A romantasy reader expects two things at once, and both must be kept.

- **A love story at the heart.** The relationship drives the book as much as the adventure. Take it away and the plot should fall apart.
- **A world that matters.** The magic, the power and the dangers create the obstacles to love, not just the backdrop.
- **A slow burn.** The tension builds over many chapters: resistance, closeness, almost, and only then something more.
- **An ending that rewards.** A happy ending, or a promise that holds to the next book in the series. A sad ending breaks the genre.
- **Stakes for both.** What is at stake in the world should also be at stake between them.

notes.title: Two arcs braided
notes.body:
This book's structure follows both arcs. Ask the same two questions of every chapter:

**What happens between them?** Resistance, being forced to work together, trust, betrayal, choice.

**What happens in the world?** The quest, the threat, the magic awakening, the power closing in on them.

The strongest chapters are those where the answers are tied together: when a turn in the world forces a turn between them, or the other way round. The midpoint is the clearest example, where the first kiss comes as the fantasy plot turns.

notes.title: Checklist for the first draft
notes.body:
Check once the draft is done:

- Do both main characters want something concrete, and do their goals stand in each other's way?
- Does the magic have rules, a price and limits, and is it never used to solve something for free?
- Does the tension between them grow in every part, even when they are apart?
- Does the betrayal have roots early in the book, so that it feels inevitable afterwards?
- Does love decide the battle, so that the two arcs meet at the end?
- Is the ending happy, or does it promise something that holds to the next book?

notes.title: Common pitfalls
notes.body:
- **Insta-love.** Let them earn each other. Attraction is not the same as love.
- **A world without a price.** Magic that always works takes the tension away.
- **Misunderstandings one talk could fix.** Give the conflict a real cause: loyalties, secrets, duty.
- **A passive main character.** She or he should choose, not just be rescued.
- **The romance vanishes in the final battle.** The grand gesture should be part of the battle, not after it.

notes.title: The main character (template)
notes.body:
Rename the note to the character's name.

**Wants:** what they chase when the book begins.

**Needs:** what they must learn to become whole.

**The wound:** what makes them afraid to trust anyone.

**The gift:** magic, heritage or skill, and what it costs.

**The secret:** what they do not want the love interest to know.

**What they risk:** in the world, and between them.

notes.title: The love interest (template)
notes.body:
Rename the note to the character's name.

**First impression:** why the main character dislikes or distrusts them.

**The other side:** what shows when the wall comes down.

**The loyalty:** who or what they serve, and why it clashes.

**The secret:** what becomes the betrayal.

**What they sacrifice at the end:** the grand gesture.

notes.title: The antagonist (template)
notes.body:
Rename the note to the character's name.

**Wants:** what the antagonist would do anything for.

**Why it makes sense:** an antagonist who is right in some way is the most dangerous.

**The threat to the relationship:** how the antagonist drives the two apart.

**The power:** what they have that the main characters lack.

notes.title: The magic system (template)
notes.body:
**Who has the magic:** and who does not.

**Rules:** what it can and cannot do.

**The price:** what each use costs.

**The limit:** what can never be done, however much is paid.

**How it ties to the love story:** a bond, a heritage or a curse that touches them both.

notes.title: Power and realms (template)
notes.body:
**The realms or courts:** who they are and what they want.

**The loyalties:** who the main characters belong to, and why it is dangerous to love across the line.

**The threat to everyone:** what forces enemies to work together.
